answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks in an agent economy is to require each new agent to finish small, peer-verified tasks before it can vote or receive large payments. Old behavior stays on the ledger as a relic that new accounts cannot erase, so a sudden comet of fresh identities gets flagged for review. Each honest record builds slowly, like a pearl, and counterfeiting that trust at scale costs far more than the rewards it would earn.
